messages:
omar: Heads-up: eu-west1 rack-7 is showing ~30% stranded GPU capacity. Nodes report free GPUs but pods stay Pending. Not a plain quota issue, looks packing/scheduler scoring related.

mia: Can you paste the scheduler events? curious if this is taint/affinity churn or a topology scoring bug. :thinking:

sasha: Quick dump from k8s events (filtered):
```
0s   Normal   FailedScheduling   pod/tiny-train-abc   0/24 nodes are available: 12 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 8 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector, 4 node(s) had insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
0s   Normal   FailedScheduling   pod/tiny-train-abc   Preemption is not helpful: no lower priority pod to evict
```

lee: Additional context: rack-7 nodes carry a soft rack-affinity label we added for locality (rack=7). Tiny pods have anti-affinity against same-pod-group to avoid noisy neighbors, which is causing scatter. Scheduler is choosing spread over binpack because our topology weight for zones/racks is high.

omar: Autoscaler didn't spin new nodes; autoscaler-bot logged a scale decision earlier: "no scale up: insufficient scheduling signal - pending pods prefer non-existent topology". It looks like the scheduler score is causing pods to prefer empty nodes on other racks, but those nodes are tainted for other workloads, so they end up unschedulable.

autoscaler-bot: [5178000008] cluster-autoscaler: scale down skipped; recent scale events present.

mia: Hypothesis: our rack-locality score is overweighted vs binpack score. For tiny pods we should prefer compact packing (lower latency / cheaper) and allow soft tolerate for the rack taint.

sasha: Agreed. Quick experiment idea: reduce topologySpread weight for rack label from 100 -> 30 for the 'tiny-pod' class and relax taint penalty in scoring plugin. That should let scheduler prefer nodes with GPUs already warm.

lee: Also we see preemption disabled for these pods (priority class low). If we enable conservative preemption or allow preemptible mixing for tiny burst pods we'll reduce stranded GPUs. But need to check latency regressions.

ana: Cost note: current fragmentation estimated ~250 GPU-hours waste/day in eu-west1 if this persists. That bumps monthly infra bill ~+$18k. We should act fast.

omar: Proposed action items:
- change scheduler config patch: topologyWeight rack=30 for tiny classes (canary on eu-west1)
- add a scheduling plugin tweak to reduce taint penalty for the "gpu-isolated" taint for tiny pods
- enable conservative preemption for tiny-pod class for 1 hour canary
- run 2-hour soak and watch eviction/latency metrics and costs

mia: I'll open a short-lived rollout PR and the canary job. tagging @eng-sre for monitoring dashboards.

sasha: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-configs/pull/412 (canary config + rollback) :thumbsup:

lee: If canary looks good, we should roll to other eu racks but keep us-west untouched until we validate network/peer link behavior. rack-locality changes can interact badly with NVLink topology.

omar: Agreed. @ana can you add alert for "stranded_gpu_percentage > 20% for 10m" and a playbook note?

ana: On it. I'll also add a cost-runbook snippet and a quick slack alert to #incidents if threshold trips.

omar: Cool. If no objections, we start canary in 10m. Otherwise call it out here.

mia: No objections from me. Starting PR deploy in 10m.

sasha: Will watch scheduler logs and post a short summary after 30m.

lee: Thanks team.

omar: Closing thread — will update with canary outcome. :white_check_mark:
